# Resource: stripe_test_helpers_test_clock

A clock that freezes time for the customers and subscriptions attached to it, so a test can move billing forward. Create it with a `frozen_time`, then attach a customer by setting the customer's `test_clock` to the clock's `id`. Setting a later `frozen_time` advances the clock in place and waits until it is `ready` again, within the update timeout; Stripe renews the subscriptions on the clock as it moves, and refuses to move it more than two billing intervals at a time. Setting an earlier one fails at plan time, because a clock never goes backwards: to start again at an earlier time, recreate the clock deliberately with `terraform taint` or by changing `name`, since `-replace` cannot get past the plan check.

~> `terraform destroy` deletes the clock, and Stripe deletes every customer attached to it and cancels their subscriptions. A subscription stays retrievable as `canceled`. Changing `name` replaces the clock, which deletes what is attached to the old one.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "stripe_test_helpers_test_clock" "billing" {
  name        = "Renewal test"
  frozen_time = 1790000000
}

resource "stripe_customer" "acme" {
  name       = "Acme GmbH"
  test_clock = stripe_test_helpers_test_clock.billing.id
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `frozen_time` - (Required) The initial frozen time for this test clock.

The following arguments are optional:

* `name` - (Optional) The name for this test clock. Changing it replaces the resource.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `deletes_after` - Time at which this clock is scheduled to auto delete.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `status` - The status of the Test Clock. Possible values: `advancing`, `internal_failure`, `ready`.
* `status_details` - See [`status_details`](#status_details) below.

<a id="status_details"></a>
### `status_details`

The `status_details` attribute supports:

* `advancing` - See [`status_details.advancing`](#status_details.advancing) below.

<a id="status_details.advancing"></a>
### `status_details.advancing`

The `status_details.advancing` attribute supports:

* `target_frozen_time` - The `frozen_time` that the Test Clock is advancing towards.

## Timeouts

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import a test helpers test clock using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_test_helpers_test_clock.billing
  id = "clock_123"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_test_helpers_test_clock.billing
  identity = {
    id = "clock_123"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the test helpers test clock.

Using `terraform import`, import a test helpers test clock using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_test_helpers_test_clock.billing clock_123
```
